MGIMS Organises National Conference on Strengthening Health Care for Tribal & Rural Women
Wednesday, 26 November 2025
1910 Hits
The Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, MGIMS, organized a three-day national conference titled “STRI Arogya: A Commemoration of the Legacy of Sadhana Tai Amte” from 21st to 23rd November 2025 at the New Auditorium, MGIMS. The conference focused on “Strengthening Health Care for Tribal and Rural Women of India by Advancing the Obstetric and Gynaecological Acumen of Rural Health Professionals.”
Dr. Nipun Vinayak (Secretary, Public Health Department, Government of Maharashtra) was the Chief Guest. The Guests of Honour were Dr. Vaishali Biniwali (Patankar Medical Foundation, Pune) and Dr. Anupama Rao (Jhpiego, New Delhi). Dr. A. K. Shukla (Dean, MGIMS) delivered the welcome address, while Dr. B. S. Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society) highlighted MGIMS’s long-standing commitment to rural healthcare innovation. Referring to Gandhiji’s call to serve the poorest, he reiterated that the institute continues to support transformative initiatives like this first-of-its-kind conference.
In his keynote address, Dr. Nipun Vinayak spoke on the intersectionality of rural and tribal women’s health and emphasized the urgent need to strengthen maternal healthcare across the country. He shared that there are currently 2.9 million pregnant women nationwide, with around 1.5 crore deliveries taking place in government hospitals, underscoring the importance of early high-risk pregnancy detection and mandatory postnatal guidance.
“Frontline nurses, midwives, and doctors are often the first and only lifeline for a mother in distress. If they are empowered, confident, and well-trained, the trajectory of maternal health can change dramatically,” said Shri P. L. Tapadiya (President, Kasturba Health Society).
The conference included expert-led sessions by senior obstetricians from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, and Bihar. Highlights included a session by Dr. V. P. Paily (Kochi) on managing C-section complications and a presentation by Dr. Dipak Desai (Mumbai) on the extra-peritoneal C-section technique for safer outcomes and reduced infection risk. Delegates engaged in hands-on training covering obstetric examinations, suturing, management of breech and shoulder dystocia, labour monitoring, newborn resuscitation, and non-pharmacological pain relief. Core discussions also centered on respectful maternity care, mental health during pregnancy, and ensuring continuum of care from home to hospital.
Dr. Poonam V. Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital) emphasized the importance of teamwork in advancing maternal health and acknowledged the Government of Maharashtra’s unwavering support for maternal and nutrition programs. She stressed that collaborative efforts among Medical Officers, Community Health Officers, and Obstetricians are vital for comprehensive and compassionate care.
The conference received technical support from Jhpiego, New Delhi, and was conducted under the aegis of LBP, BHS, JSS, and the Government of Maharashtra.
